design:
## Design tests

Each change was read first on the isolation bench (`vision/isolation_v015.md`): the template forced alone into a picture, cut out with nothing else around it and read blind by a fresh reader, two rounds and 36 images. The bench caught a girl on the swing whose hands stuck out wider than the ropes ("arms could also be read as stretched straight out"); a walking skirt with "a darker blue blob near its lower part" and legs that "cross each other in an X shape" (the lobes were flattened at the back, and the walkers with an ice cream or a balloon now walk side on); a bird's branch that "floats inside the canopy ... pasted onto the green leaf mass"; a bird table that "could be ... a garden lamp or lantern"; and a sleeping cat "in the middle of the tiled pavement". It also kept two seesaw poses first marked for retirement: a bench picture showed a teenager riding the seesaw with them when both children were busy.

The refined visuals were then read blind in six whole test scenes among other events (`vision/design_tests_v015.md`). The wave read as a wave in all five scenes that had one, aimed each time at someone simply going about their day ("raises one hand high in a wave; little motion marks around the hand show it is moving"); the walker reading toward a bucket read as "about to walk into it or trip over it"; the blocked hose in full ("when the dog steps off, water may suddenly gush out"). No reader saw a leg apart from a body, closed eyes on a chore, a hose across a path, a bush or a bird table behind the fence, or washing hanging still beside a kite.

Building the tier-4 pictures changed one rule: the obstacle in front of a walker about to trip is set no higher than the ground under the leading foot (it could land above the walkable ground, and the picture would not place). The three pictures already built with that event rebuilt identically.
intro: The wave, the one template that failed the v0.14 gate, passes the twelfth screen with full marks in all three of its pictures, a waving child among them ("smiling and waving one raised hand, with small lines by her hand showing the waving motion"). For the first time no item in the whole screen was misread, set or probes: 731 of 738 scored items had full marks. No reader saw a gap in anyone's body. The set scored 0.988 over all items (0.995 in v0.14) with 1.4 unintended oddities per picture, and 61 of 64 templates pass the gate. The three that fall short each lost their points in a single set picture where something beside them drew the reading away: a stalking cat with a second cat walking the same fence behind it, read as "just walking along"; a girl stuck on the seesaw in a busy picture, read as ordinary play; and a bird on the fence just under the clothesline, read as perched on the line.
screen: Across all 62 pictures only 7 of 738 scored items fell short of full marks (4 of 703 in v0.14) and none was misread: in the set, three in a tier-4 garden isomorph (the stalking cat, and a pointing hand raised beside it), two in a tier-3 playground isomorph (the stuck girl) and one in a tier-3 garden picture (the bird on the fence); in the probes, one half point on a begging dog. Unintended oddities held at 29 in the set (28 in v0.14) and fell from 47 to 39 in the probes. None of the v0.14 oddities came back as reported then: the washing lifts in a kite's breeze, the bushes and the bird table stand in front of the fence, no hose crosses a path, no chore face looks closed, no lost balloon shares a colour, no cat sleeps on the pavement, no picnic or sprinkler runs under storm clouds, and the swing's hands hold its ropes. What remains is mostly placement: someone at the back drawn too big for the distance, unrelated things touching (a goat "partly through" a woman's legs, a door knob "on the dog's head"), walkers heading for something that is not their event ("might trip over" a hose), and the square-wheeled bicycle "standing on its own" again.
redrawn: The wave reads in all three of its pictures, the waving child among them. The visuals redrawn or moved for the v0.14 oddities read with full marks wherever they were screened: the walker about to trip in all six of its pictures (0.93 in v0.14), the lost balloon in all four, the sprinkler and its wet package in all three, and the kite flyer, the swing, the sweep and the rake in all three each. The perched bird lost half a point once, on the fence under the clothesline (below).
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (48 in three, 10 in four, 3 in five, 3 in six). Three fail, none on a misread and each on a single set picture: the stalking cat (0.89), the heavy man on the seesaw (0.88) and the perched bird (0.83). The v0.16 fixes: no second cat on the fence a cat is stalking along, and pointing hands kept clear of animals they do not point at; the stuck girl without the motion lines at her feet and calling down to the man, read on the bench first; no bird on the fence under a clothesline.
